name: Kanda Poha
steps: Wash the flattened rice (poha) gently and drain completely. Let it rest.
Heat oil in a pan, add mustard seeds, peanuts, and sauté until the peanuts are crunchy.
Add chopped onions and green chillies; sauté until the onions are translucent.
Stir in turmeric and salt, then add the soaked poha and mix well.
Cover and steam for 2-3 minutes on low heat.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon juice and garnish with fresh coriander.

name: Kanda Batata Poha
steps: Prepare poha by washing and draining.
Dice potatoes into small cubes and fry them in oil until golden and soft.
In the same pan, add mustard, onions, and green chillies; sauté well.
Add the fried potatoes, turmeric, and salt.
Toss in the poha, mix gently, and steam for 2 minutes.
Serve hot with a garnish of grated coconut.

name: Upma (Rava)
steps: Dry roast semolina (rava) until it becomes aromatic and slightly golden.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds, urad dal, and curry leaves.
Add chopped onions, green chillies, and grated ginger; sauté until soft.
Pour in 3 cups of water for every 1 cup of rava and add salt.
Once the water boils, add the roasted rava slowly while stirring to prevent lumps.
Cover and cook on low flame for 5 minutes until fluffy.

name: Sabudana Khichdi
steps: Wash sabudana and soak it with just enough water to cover it for 5-6 hours.
Mix roasted and coarsely ground peanut powder, salt, and a pinch of sugar into the soaked sabudana.
Heat ghee in a pan, add cumin seeds and diced potatoes; cook until the potatoes are tender.
Add chopped green chillies and the sabudana mixture.
Sauté on medium-high heat until the pearls become translucent.
Garnish with lemon juice and serve immediately.

name: Thalipeeth
steps: Prepare a dough by mixing bhajani (multigrain) flour with finely chopped onions, coriander, and chillies.
Add cumin seeds and salt; knead into a soft dough using warm water.
Grease a damp cloth or a plastic sheet and pat a ball of dough into a thin circle.
Transfer to a hot griddle (tawa) and make a hole in the center.
Drizzle oil in the center and around the edges; cook until golden brown on both sides.
Serve with homemade white butter (loni).

name: Misal Pav
steps: Boil sprouted moth beans (matki) with turmeric and salt.
Prepare a 'vatan' (paste) by roasting onions and dry coconut until dark brown and grinding them.
Heat oil, sauté ginger-garlic paste and the vatan until the oil separates.
Add misal masala and the boiled sprouts with their water.
Simmer until a thick layer of 'kat' (oil) forms on top.
Serve the spicy curry (usal) topped with farsan, onions, and lemon with pav.

name: Batata Bhaji
steps: Dice boiled and peeled potatoes into cubes.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds, cumin, and curry leaves.
Add slit green chillies and turmeric.
Add the potato cubes and salt; toss well to coat.
Cook covered for 3 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve with hot puris.

name: Dapanyache Pohe
steps: Wash the poha and drain water; mix with salt, sugar, and plenty of fresh grated coconut.
Let the mixture sit for 10 minutes to absorb the coconut moisture.
Heat oil and prepare a tempering of mustard seeds, hing, and green chillies.
Pour the hot tempering over the poha mixture and toss gently.
Cover and let the flavors meld for 5 minutes without further cooking.
Serve with a final squeeze of lemon juice.

name: Sanja
steps: Dry roast rava on low flame until it turns aromatic.
Heat oil and temper with mustard seeds, cumin, and curry leaves.
Sauté chopped onions and green chillies until soft.
Add turmeric and a little red chilli powder for a spicy kick.
Add boiling water and salt, then stir in the roasted rava.
Cook covered on low flame until the water is fully absorbed and the sanja is fluffy.

name: Ghavan
steps: Mix rice flour and salt with enough water to make a very thin, watery batter.
Heat a non-stick or cast iron tawa and grease it lightly.
Pour a ladleful of batter quickly from the edges toward the center.
Cover with a lid and cook for 1 minute until it becomes spongy.
Fold and remove without flipping.
Serve warm with coconut chutney or jaggery mixed with coconut milk.

name: Amboli
steps: Soak rice and urad dal with fenugreek seeds for 6 hours.
Grind into a smooth batter and ferment overnight.
The batter should be thick yet pourable.
Pour a ladleful on a hot tawa and spread slightly thicker than a regular dosa.
Cover and cook until the base is golden and the top is porous.
Serve with spicy chutney or usal.

name: Jwariche Dhirde
steps: Mix jowar (sorghum) flour with chopped onions, green chillies, and spices.
Add water to create a batter of pouring consistency.
Heat a pan and drizzle oil.
Pour the batter and spread in a thin circle.
Cook on medium flame until crisp and golden brown on both sides.
Serve hot with curd or pickle.

name: Zunka
steps: Heat oil and add mustard seeds, lots of crushed garlic, and green chillies.
Add chopped onions and sauté until brown.
Sprinkle besan (gram flour) over the onions while stirring continuously.
Add salt, turmeric, and a little water to moisten the flour.
Cover and steam for 5 minutes until the besan is cooked and dry.
Garnish with coriander and serve with Jowar Bhakri.

name: Pithla
steps: Whisk besan with water to form a smooth, lump-free slurry.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds, and sauté crushed garlic and chillies.
Add turmeric and pour the besan slurry into the pan.
Cook while stirring constantly until the mixture thickens to a custard-like consistency.
Simmer for 3 minutes on low heat.
Serve hot as a comforting gravy with Bhakri or Rice.

name: Modak (Steamed)
steps: Prepare the filling by cooking grated coconut and jaggery together until thickened.
Add cardamom powder and let the filling cool.
Boil water with a pinch of salt and ghee; add rice flour and mix quickly to form a dough.
Knead the warm dough until smooth.
Shape small portions into bowls, stuff with filling, and pleat the edges to form a cone.
Steam for 10 minutes and serve with a dollop of ghee.

name: Kurdai
steps: Soak wheat for 3 days, extracting the milk-like starch daily.
Boil water with salt and add the starch, stirring vigorously to form a thick, glossy paste.
While hot, press the paste through a sev-maker to form thin rings.
Sun-dry the rings completely for 2-3 days until they become brittle.
Store in an airtight container.
Deep fry when needed; they will puff up into white, crispy nests.

name: Alu Vadi
steps: Prepare a thick paste of besan, tamarind, jaggery, and spices.
Wash colocasia leaves and remove the thick veins.
Apply the paste on the back of one leaf, place another on top, and repeat.
Roll the leaves tightly and steam for 20 minutes.
Slice the rolls into wheels once cooled.
Shallow fry or deep fry until crispy and serve as a snack.

name: Rava Sheera
steps: Heat ghee in a pan and roast semolina (rava) until golden and fragrant.
In another pot, boil milk and water together.
Slowly pour the hot liquid into the rava while stirring continuously.
Add sugar and cardamom powder once the liquid is absorbed.
Cover and cook for 2 minutes; garnish with fried cashews and raisins.
Serve warm as a sweet breakfast or dessert.

name: Bread Upma
steps: Cut bread slices into small cubes.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds, onions, and chillies; sauté until soft.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until mushy.
Stir in turmeric and salt, then add the bread cubes.
Toss well until the bread is coated and slightly toasted.
Garnish with coriander and serve hot.

name: Rava Idli
steps: Roast rava slightly and let it cool.
Mix with curd, grated carrots, ginger, and salt to form a thick batter.
Let the batter rest for 15 minutes.
Just before steaming, add a pinch of eno (fruit salt) and mix gently.
Pour into greased idli moulds.
Steam for 10-12 minutes until soft and fluffy.

name: Sabudana Vada
steps: Soak sabudana for 5-6 hours until soft.
Mix with boiled and mashed potatoes, crushed peanuts, and chillies.
Add cumin seeds and salt; knead into a cohesive mixture.
Shape into small flat patties.
Deep fry in hot oil on medium-low flame until golden brown and crispy.
Serve with sweetened curd or peanut chutney.

name: Puran Poli
steps: Boil chana dal until soft, then grind with jaggery and cardamom to make the sweet stuffing (puran).
Prepare a soft, elastic dough using wheat flour, oil, and water.
Stuff a ball of puran into the dough and seal tightly.
Roll it out into a thin circle using rice flour for dusting.
Cook on a hot griddle with plenty of ghee until golden spots appear.
Serve hot with a side of milk or katachi amti.

name: Matki Usal
steps: Heat oil, add mustard seeds, and sauté onions until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and godamasala.
Toss in the sprouted moth beans and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add a little water and salt; cover and cook until the beans are tender.
Garnish with grated coconut and coriander.
Serve as a healthy breakfast or lunch side.

name: Bhakri
steps: Mix jowar (sorghum) flour with salt and enough boiling water to form a soft dough.
Knead the dough well while it is still warm until smooth.
Pat a portion into a flat circle using your hands on a floured surface.
Transfer to a hot tawa; apply water on the top surface with a cloth.
Flip and cook the other side until it puffs up over direct flame.
Serve with Pithla or a spicy chutney.

name: Gharge
steps: Steam or boil yellow pumpkin and mash it smoothly.
Mix the mash with melted jaggery and wheat flour to form a stiff dough.
Add a pinch of salt to enhance the flavor.
Roll out small discs like pooris.
Deep fry in hot oil until they puff up and turn dark golden brown.
Enjoy these sweet and savory fritters as a travel snack or breakfast.

name: Varan Bhaat
steps: Pressure cook toor dal with turmeric and a drop of oil until mushy.
Wash and cook rice until grains are separate and fluffy.
Whisk the cooked dal thoroughly with a hand blender or whisk.
Add salt and water to adjust the dal to a pourable consistency.
Serve the plain dal over hot rice and top with a generous dollop of ghee.

name: Amti
steps: Whisk cooked and mashed toor dal until smooth.
Add kokum for tanginess, jaggery for sweetness, and godamasala.
Heat oil and prepare a tempering with mustard seeds, curry leaves, and hing.
Pour the tempering into the dal and bring to a rolling boil.
Simmer for 10 minutes to let the flavors balance and garnish with coriander.

name: Zunka Bhakri
steps: Prepare dry Zunka by sautéing chopped onions, garlic, and green chillies in oil.
Slowly stir in besan and cook until it absorbs the oil and turns aromatic.
Serve the hot Zunka with freshly made Jowar or Bajra Bhakri.
Accompany with spicy green chilli Thecha and raw onion slices.

name: Pithla Bhakri
steps: Prepare a semi-liquid gram flour gravy (Pithla) with plenty of garlic and green chillies.
Serve as a comforting, thick gravy alongside warm Bhakri.
Drizzle a teaspoon of raw oil over the Pithla for extra flavor.
Pairs traditionally with a side of fresh koshimbir or spicy pickle.

name: Bharli Vangi
steps: Slit small purple brinjals into four segments without removing the stem.
Mix roasted peanut powder, coconut, godamasala, and salt to create the stuffing.
Stuff the masala tightly into each brinjal and sauté in oil until charred.
Add a little water and cook covered on low flame until the brinjals are tender.

name: Walachi Usal
steps: Peel the bitter skins off sprouted field beans (dalimbi).
Sauté onions with Malvani or Godamasala in hot oil.
Add the peeled beans, tamarind paste, and a bit of jaggery.
Cook until the beans are soft and garnish with grated coconut and coriander.

name: Kobichi Bhaji
steps: Soak chana dal for 30 minutes before starting.
Heat oil and temper with mustard seeds and slit green chillies.
Add shredded cabbage, soaked dal, turmeric, and salt.
Steam-cook without adding water to maintain a slight crunch in the cabbage.

name: Koshimbir
steps: Finely chop cucumber and mix with crushed, roasted peanut powder.
Add curd or lemon juice, sugar, and salt to taste.
Prepare a tempering of mustard seeds and green chillies.
Pour the tempering over the cucumber and serve chilled.

name: Bharli Tondli
steps: Slit ivy gourds (tondli) lengthwise into four segments.
Stuff with a spicy mix of peanut powder, turmeric, and godamasala.
Sauté in oil on low flame and add a dash of water.
Cook covered until the gourds shrivel and become soft and caramelized.

name: Chapati (Poli)
steps: Knead wheat flour with oil and salt into a soft, smooth dough.
Rest the dough for 15 minutes, then divide into small balls.
Roll into thin circles and roast on a hot tawa with oil or ghee.
Stack the soft, puffed chapatis in a container to keep them warm.

name: Rice
steps: Wash rice until the water runs clear and use a 1:2 ratio of rice to water.
Cook in a pressure cooker for 3 whistles or in a pot until fluffy.
Rest the rice for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork.
Serve hot as the primary grain for lunch meals.

name: Shev Bhaji
steps: Grind roasted onions and dry coconut into a smooth, spicy paste.
Sauté the paste until the oil separates and turns into a fiery red gravy.
Add water and simmer to create a thin rassa.
Add thick, spicy sev just before serving to avoid sogginess.

name: Aluchi Bhaji
steps: Pressure cook chopped colocasia leaves with peanuts and chana dal.
Mash the mixture and add tamarind juice, jaggery, and godamasala.
Add a tempering of mustard, cumin, and plenty of crushed garlic.
Simmer until the dish reaches a sweet, sour, and spicy balance.

name: Vangyache Bharit
steps: Roast a large brinjal over an open flame until charred and soft.
Peel and mash the pulp, then sauté with onions, ginger, and chillies.
Cook for 2 minutes to let the smoky flavor infuse.
Garnish with plenty of fresh coriander before serving.

name: Kadhi
steps: Whisk curd with besan and water until smooth.
Prepare a tempering with ghee, mustard seeds, and curry leaves.
Add ginger-garlic paste and pour in the curd mixture while stirring.
Simmer on low heat until it just begins to boil.

name: Solkadhi
steps: Extract deep pink juice from soaked kokum petals.
Mix the kokum extract with fresh coconut milk.
Add a crushed paste of garlic and green chillies.
Serve chilled as a digestive drink or with rice.

name: Tambda Rassa
steps: Grind roasted spices, onions, and coconut into a fine paste.
Sauté the paste until the oil turns bright red and separates.
Add water and simmer into a thin, spicy broth.
Serve as a fiery red accompaniment to lunch thalis.

name: Pandhra Rassa
steps: Grind cashews and poppy seeds into a rich white paste.
Infuse broth with whole spices like cinnamon and cardamom.
Stir in the paste and fresh coconut milk; simmer gently.
Season with salt to create a creamy, white, mildly spiced gravy.

name: Hirvya Vatanyachi Usal
steps: Sauté onions until translucent and add ginger-garlic paste and peas.
Stir in turmeric, chilli powder, salt, and a little water.
Cover and cook until the peas are tender.
Garnish with grated coconut and fresh coriander.

name: Thecha
steps: Dry roast green chillies and garlic on a tawa until charred.
Add a little oil and sauté briefly, then crush coarsely in a mortar.
Add salt and a dash of lemon juice.
Enjoy as a spicy condiment with hot Bhakri.

name: Bajra Bhakri
steps: Knead bajra flour with hot water until smooth and pliable.
Pat the dough into a thin circle on a floured surface.
Roast on a tawa, dabbing the top with water until it puffs.
Traditionally eaten with Pithla or Thecha during winter.

name: Chavali Usal
steps: Pressure cook soaked black-eyed peas until tender.
Sauté onions and tomatoes with ginger-garlic paste and godamasala.
Add the cooked beans and simmer until the gravy thickens.
Garnish with coriander and serve with Poli or Rice.

name: Gola Bhaat
steps: Prepare and steam small gole (balls) made of spiced besan.
Sauté rice with onions, godamasala, and vegetables.
Add the steamed gole to the rice and cook together.
Serve hot with a side of curd or pickle.

name: Methi Chi Bhaji
steps: Clean and chop fenugreek leaves and soak moong dal briefly.
Sauté plenty of garlic and green chillies in oil.
Add the methi and dal; cook without covering to keep it green.
Serve as a healthy lunch side with Chapati.

name: Dalimbi Usal
steps: Sauté onions and spices, then add peeled dalimbi beans.
Add tamarind paste and jaggery; simmer until the beans are tender.
Finish with a layer of grated coconut.
Often served at festive occasions and weddings.

name: Kanda Bhaji
steps: Slice onions thinly and mix with salt; let them rest for 10 minutes to release water.
Add chopped green chillies, coriander, and ajwain seeds.
Slowly mix in besan (gram flour) without adding extra water, until the onions are coated.
Heat oil for deep frying.
Drop small, irregular portions of the mixture into hot oil.
Fry until golden brown and extra crispy; serve with green chutney.

name: Batata Vada
steps: Mash boiled potatoes and temper with mustard, garlic, and curry leaves.
Roll the mixture into balls.
Dip in a turmeric-tinted besan batter.
Deep fry until golden.
Serve hot as a standalone snack or inside a pav.
The ultimate Mumbai street food.

name: Suralichi Vadi
steps: Whisk besan and buttermilk with turmeric and salt into a smooth batter.
Cook the mixture on low flame, stirring constantly until it becomes thick and glossy.
Quickly spread the hot paste thinly over the back of greased plates.
Once cooled, cut into strips and roll them tightly into small cylinders.
Temper with mustard seeds and green chillies.
Garnish with fresh coconut and coriander.

name: Bhel Puri
steps: Mix puffed rice (kurmura) with chopped onions, boiled potatoes, and tomatoes.
Add tangy tamarind chutney and spicy green chutney.
Toss well with a pinch of chaat masala and salt.
Top with a generous amount of sev and pomegranate arils.
Garnish with coriander and serve immediately before it gets soggy.
A quintessential beach snack from Mumbai.

name: Shev Chivda
steps: Deep fry peanuts, roasted gram, and thin slices of dry coconut until golden.
Fry curry leaves until crispy.
Mix the fried ingredients with thick or thin sev.
Add salt, turmeric, and a pinch of sugar for a sweet-savory balance.
Toss well while the ingredients are still slightly warm.
Store in an airtight container for a crunchy tea-time snack.

name: Poha Chivda
steps: Dry roast thin flattened rice (poha) on low flame until it becomes crisp.
Heat oil and fry peanuts, roasted gram, and green chillies.
Add turmeric and salt to the oil, then pour it over the roasted poha.
Mix gently to avoid breaking the poha flakes.
Add powdered sugar for a hint of sweetness.
A healthy, roasted snack common during Diwali.

name: Kothimbir Vadi
steps: Mix a large amount of finely chopped coriander with besan, crushed peanuts, and spices.
Add a little water to form a thick, steamable batter.
Steam the mixture in a tray for 15-20 minutes.
Once cooled, cut into squares or diamond shapes.
Shallow fry or deep fry until the edges are crispy and golden.
Serve with tomato ketchup or green chutney.

name: Thalipeeth Ladoo
steps: Dry roast thalipeeth bhajani flour until it turns aromatic and golden brown.
Melt jaggery with a little ghee and water to make a syrup.
Mix the roasted flour and cardamom powder into the warm syrup.
Add chopped nuts and mix well.
While the mixture is still warm, shape it into round balls (ladoos).
A nutritious, energy-boosting snack for kids.

name: Shakarpara
steps: Melt sugar in warm milk and add ghee.
Knead with maida (all-purpose flour) and a pinch of salt to form a stiff dough.
Roll the dough into a thick sheet.
Cut into small diamond or square shapes.
Deep fry on low heat until they turn a light golden color and become crisp.
Store as a crunchy sweet snack.

name: Bhadang
steps: Heat a large quantity of oil and sauté crushed garlic cloves with their skin until dark brown.
Fry peanuts and curry leaves until crunchy.
Add turmeric, salt, and lots of red chilli powder.
Immediately add puffed rice and toss vigorously until every grain is coated.
The heat from the oil will make the puffed rice extra crunchy.
A spicy specialty from Kolhapur.

name: Khamang Kakdi
steps: Finely chop cucumbers and squeeze out any excess water.
Mix with roasted and coarsely crushed peanut powder.
Add chopped green chillies, coriander, and a pinch of sugar.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice and add salt just before serving.
Temper with mustard seeds and cumin if desired.
A healthy, cooling salad-snack.

name: Patal Pohe Chivda
steps: Dry roast thin poha (patal pohe) until very crisp.
Prepare a tempering with mustard seeds, peanuts, and coconut slices.
Add turmeric and salt to the tempering.
Toss the poha into the pan and mix gently.
Finish with a dusting of powdered sugar and salt.
A light and popular tea-time accompaniment.

name: Shev Puri
steps: Arrange flat puris on a plate.
Top each with mashed potatoes, chopped onions, and tomatoes.
Drizzle green chilli chutney, tamarind chutney, and garlic chutney.
Cover each puri with a mountain of fine sev.
Garnish with coriander and a squeeze of lemon.
Serve immediately to enjoy the crunch.

name: Dahi Puri
steps: Gently break the top of hollow puris (pani puris).
Stuff with mashed potatoes and boiled moong or chickpeas.
Drizzle sweet and spicy chutneys inside.
Fill each puri with chilled, sweetened whisked curd.
Garnish with sev, pomegranate, and coriander.
A sweet and tangy street food delight.

name: Karanji
steps: Prepare a stuffing of grated dry coconut, roasted poppy seeds, jaggery, and cardamom.
Make a dough with maida, ghee, and milk.
Roll out small discs, place a spoonful of stuffing, and fold into a semi-circle.
Seal the edges using a fork or a cutter.
Deep fry until golden and crispy.
A traditional sweet made during Diwali and Holi.

name: Chakli
steps: Knead bhajani flour (roasted multigrain flour) with butter, sesame seeds, and spices using hot water.
The dough should be firm yet soft enough to pass through a press.
Use a chakli press to form spiral shapes on a sheet.
Deep fry on medium flame until they stop bubbling and turn dark golden.
Drain and cool; they become very crunchy once cold.
Store in an airtight container for weeks.

name: Shankarpali (Savory)
steps: Knead maida with ghee, cumin seeds, ajwain, and salt using water.
Roll into a thick circle.
Cut into small squares or diamonds.
Deep fry on low to medium flame until they puff slightly and become golden.
A popular savory counterpart to the sweet shakarpara.
Perfect for snacking with tea.

name: Anarse
steps: Soak rice for 3 days, changing water daily. Dry and grind into a fine powder.
Mix the rice flour with equal parts jaggery and rest for 2 days.
Shape small balls and press them onto a bed of poppy seeds (khaskhas).
Shallow fry in ghee on one side only while splashing hot ghee on top.
The side with poppy seeds should be on top.
Drain the mesh-like sweet and let the oil drip before storing.

name: Bakarwadi
steps: Prepare a spicy, sweet, and tangy stuffing with poppy seeds, coconut, and tamarind.
Make a dough using maida and besan.
Roll the dough thin, spread the stuffing, and roll it up tightly like a log.
Slice into small bite-sized rounds.
Deep fry on low heat until very crispy.
A famous specialty from Pune known for its complex flavor profile.

name: Tilgul
steps: Dry roast sesame seeds (til) and crushed peanuts.
Melt jaggery until it reaches a soft-ball consistency.
Quickly mix in the sesame seeds, peanuts, and coconut.
While the mixture is still hot, grease your palms and roll into small round balls.
Exchange these balls during Makar Sankranti as a sign of goodwill.
A healthy winter snack high in calcium and energy.

name: Vada Pav
steps: Mash boiled potatoes with a tempering of mustard, garlic-chilli paste, and turmeric.
Shape the mixture into medium-sized balls.
Dip each ball into a thick batter made of besan (gram flour), salt, and turmeric.
Deep fry until the outer layer is crispy and golden.
Slice a pav, apply dry garlic chutney inside, and place the vada.
Serve hot with a fried green chilli.

name: Pav Bhaji
steps: Boil and mash potatoes, peas, and cauliflower until smooth.
Heat butter in a large pan; sauté chopped onions until translucent.
Add ginger-garlic paste and chopped tomatoes; cook until mushy.
Mix in pav bhaji masala, red chilli powder, and salt.
Add the mashed vegetables and a splash of water; mash further while cooking.
Finish with a large dollop of butter and serve with buttered pav.

name: Sabudana Vada
steps: Soak sabudana for 5-6 hours until soft.
Mix with boiled and mashed potatoes, crushed peanuts, and chillies.
Add cumin seeds and salt; knead into a cohesive mixture.
Shape into small flat patties.
Deep fry in hot oil on medium-low flame until golden brown and crispy.
Serve with sweetened curd or peanut chutney.

name: Pohe Ladoo
steps: Dry roast poha until it becomes very crisp, then grind it into a coarse powder.
Mix with grated jaggery and cardamom powder.
Add warm melted ghee until the mixture can be shaped.
Toss in some fried cashews and raisins.
Roll into round balls.
A quick and healthy sweet snack made with minimal ingredients.

name: Upwas Thalipeeth
steps: Soak sabudana and mix with rajgira (amaranth) flour.
Add boiled mashed potatoes, crushed peanuts, and chillies.
Knead into a dough and pat onto a greased sheet into circles.
Cook on a tawa with ghee until both sides are golden and crispy.
Serve with peanut chutney or sweetened curd during fasting days.
A wholesome and filling upwas snack.

name: Moong Dal Khichdi
steps: Wash rice and moong dal together; soak for 20 minutes.
Heat ghee in a pressure cooker and add cumin, peppercorns, and grated ginger.
Add the soaked rice and dal with double the amount of water and salt.
Pressure cook for 3-4 whistles until very soft and mushy.
Drizzle extra ghee on top before serving.
A light and nutritious dinner perfect for easy digestion.

name: Kala Vatana Amti
steps: Soak black peas (kala vatana) overnight and pressure cook until soft.
Prepare a dark brown masala (vatan) by roasting onions and dry coconut.
Heat oil and sauté the masala until it releases oil.
Add Malvani or Godamasala and the cooked black peas.
Simmer for 15 minutes to let the gravy thicken and darken.
Serve with Amboli or Bhakri.

name: Dudhi Chi Bhaji
steps: Peel and dice bottle gourd (dudhi) into small cubes.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds and sauté chopped green chillies.
Add the bottle gourd and a handful of soaked chana dal.
Season with salt and a pinch of sugar; steam-cook until tender.
Garnish with fresh grated coconut.
A simple and healthy everyday vegetable dish.

name: Shevga Chi Bhaji
steps: Cut drumsticks into 2-inch pieces and boil them slightly.
Sauté onions and spices in oil.
Add the drumsticks and roasted peanut powder.
Stir in a little tamarind juice for tanginess.
Cook until the drumsticks are tender and the gravy is flavorful.
Serve with hot Chapatis.

name: Multigrain Bhakri
steps: Mix jowar, bajra, and nachni (ragi) flours in equal proportions.
Knead with hot water to form a soft, smooth dough.
Pat into a thin circle using your palms.
Cook on a hot tawa with a splash of water on top.
Roast on both sides until it puffs up.
A highly nutritious, gluten-free dinner bread.

name: Batata Rassa
steps: Cut potatoes into large chunks.
Heat oil and sauté onions until brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste, godamasala, and red chilli powder.
Add the potato chunks and enough water to create a thin gravy (rassa).
Pressure cook for 2 whistles until the potatoes are soft.
Garnish with coriander and serve with Rice or Chapati.

name: Boondi Raita
steps: Whisk chilled curd until smooth.
Add roasted cumin powder, black salt, and a pinch of sugar.
Stir in crispy boondi (fried gram flour drops).
Let the boondi soak for 5 minutes to become soft.
Garnish with fresh coriander.
A cooling accompaniment to spicy Maharashtrian dinners.

name: Roasted Brinjal Bharta
steps: Roast a large brinjal on direct flame until smoky and tender.
Peel the charred skin and mash the pulp.
In a pan, sauté lots of garlic, green chillies, and onions.
Stir in the mashed brinjal and cook for 5 minutes.
Add salt and a squeeze of lemon.
Serve hot with Bhakri.

name: Shev Bhaji Rassa
steps: Prepare a thin, spicy red gravy using roasted onion and coconut paste.
Simmer the gravy with godamasala and red chilli powder.
Add a handful of thick, spicy gathiya or sev just before eating.
The sev adds texture and absorbs the spicy flavors of the rassa.
Best enjoyed with soft white bread (pav).
A spicy and satisfying dinner option.

name: Patal Bhaji
steps: Pressure cook chopped spinach with soaked chana dal and peanuts.
Mash the mixture into a creamy consistency.
Add tamarind, jaggery, and godamasala for a balanced flavor.
Temper with lots of crushed garlic and mustard seeds in oil.
The gravy should be smooth and thick.
Serve hot with Rice.

name: Phodnicha Bhaat
steps: Crumble leftover rice to separate the grains.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds, peanuts, and curry leaves.
Sauté chopped onions and green chillies until golden.
Add turmeric and salt, then toss in the rice.
Mix well and steam for 3 minutes on low heat.
Garnish with coriander and serve as a quick dinner.

name: Dashmi
steps: Dissolve jaggery in warm milk.
Knead wheat flour with the jaggery-milk mixture and a little ghee.
Roll into thick circles like parathas.
Roast on a tawa with ghee until golden brown spots appear.
The result is a soft, sweet, and aromatic flatbread.
Often served with spicy pickle or plain curd.

name: Vatana Usal
steps: Soak dried green peas overnight and pressure cook until tender.
Sauté onions and tomatoes in oil until mushy.
Add godamasala and the cooked peas.
Simmer until the flavors meld and the gravy is thick.
Finish with fresh coconut and coriander.
A classic Maharashtrian legume curry.

name: Kadhi Maharashtrian
steps: Mix sour curd with besan and water; whisk until lump-free.
Prepare a tempering with ghee, mustard, cumin, and curry leaves.
Add crushed ginger and chillies.
Pour the curd mixture into the tempering and simmer gently.
Do not let it boil vigorously to avoid curdling.
Serve as a light gravy with Khichdi or Rice.

name: Shrikhand
steps: Tie thick curd in a muslin cloth and hang it for 6 hours to drain all whey (chakka).
Whisk the thick chakka with powdered sugar until smooth and creamy.
Infuse with saffron strands dissolved in warm milk.
Add cardamom powder and chopped nuts.
Chill in the refrigerator before serving.
A royal dessert often served with hot puris in a dinner meal.

name: Lasun Chatni
steps: Dry roast garlic cloves and dry coconut pieces until golden.
Add red chilli powder and salt.
Grind the mixture into a coarse powder.
This dry chutney has a long shelf life.
It adds a punch of garlic flavor to any meal.
Commonly paired with Vada Pav or Bhakri.

name: Veg Kolhapuri
steps: Roast dry coconut, sesame seeds, and poppy seeds; grind into a paste.
Sauté mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, peas, cauliflower) until tender.
Cook the coconut paste in oil with a fiery Kolhapuri masala.
Stir in the vegetables and simmer with a little water.
The dish should be bright red and very spicy.
Garnish with coriander and serve with Paratha.

name: Chavali Chi Amti
steps: Cook black-eyed peas until soft but whole.
Prepare a thin gravy using tamarind, jaggery, and godamasala.
Add a paste of fresh coconut and cumin.
Simmer for 10 minutes to allow the peas to absorb the spicy-tangy liquid.
Temper with mustard seeds and hing.
A delicious and light legume curry for dinner.

name: Mugachi Gathi
steps: Sauté sprouted moong in oil with mustard seeds and hing.
Add a paste of fresh coconut, ginger, and green chillies.
Simmer with a little water until the moong is tender.
Do not overcook; the sprouts should be soft but distinct.
A nutritious Konkani dish served as a side.
Best paired with Rice or Bhakri.

name: Gulachi Poli
steps: Prepare a stuffing with roasted sesame seeds, jaggery, and roasted gram flour.
Enclose the stuffing in a soft wheat flour dough ball.
Roll into a thin circle using plenty of flour to prevent sticking.
Roast on a hot tawa with ghee until it puffs up and turns golden.
The jaggery melts inside to form a delicious sweet layer.
A healthy and energy-dense dinner sweet.

name: Vangi Bhaat
steps: Fresh Powder: Dry roast chana dal, coriander seeds, 2 cloves, a small cinnamon stick, and 4 red chillies; grind into a coarse powder.
Cook rice grains so they are separate and spread to cool.
Sauté peanuts, mustard seeds, and sliced green brinjal in oil.
Add the prepared spice powder, salt, and a dash of tamarind juice.
Cook until brinjal is soft and the oil separates from the masala.
Gently fold the cooled rice into the brinjal masala.
Turn off the flame and rest for 2 minutes before serving.

name: Metkut Bhaat
steps: Cook rice until soft and fluffy.
Metkut is a special powder made by roasting and grinding various pulses and grains.
Mix 1-2 spoons of metkut powder into hot rice.
Add a generous amount of warm ghee and a pinch of salt.
Mix thoroughly until the rice is coated and turns light yellow.
A simple, aromatic, and easy-to-digest traditional Maharashtrian dinner.

name: Mirchi Bhaji
steps: Slit long green chillies and remove seeds if too spicy.
Prepare a thick batter of besan, ajwain, turmeric, and salt.
Dip each chilli to coat it completely.
Deep fry in hot oil until the coating is golden and crisp.
Serve as a crunchy side dish for dinner.
Adds a spicy kick to a plain dal-rice meal.

name: Amrakhand
steps: Start with thick hung curd (chakka).
Mix with fresh mango pulp and powdered sugar.
Whisk until creamy and smooth.
Add cardamom powder for aroma.
Chill thoroughly before serving.
A delicious variation of shrikhand that celebrates the mango season.

name: Saoji Veg Curry
steps: Prepare a potent Saoji masala using roasted whole spices and dry coconut.
Sauté onions and lots of garlic until dark brown.
Add the masala and cook with plenty of oil until it separates.
Add boiled vegetables and simmer for 15 minutes.
This Vidarbha specialty is famous for its extreme spice and depth of flavor.
Serve with Bhakri or Rice to balance the heat.
